title: PVTSizing: A TuRBO-RL-Based Batch-Sampling Optimization Framework for PVT-Robust Analog Circuit Synthesis
problem: Existing analog/mixed-signal design automation tools suffer from performance degradation caused by process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations. Traditional circuit sizing approaches fail to adequately optimize for robustness across PVT corners and random mismatch conditions.
motivation: As CMOS technology advances and circuit complexity grows, automated design tools that efficiently handle PVT-robust analog circuit optimization are increasingly critical.
method: PVTSizing combines two optimization methods: TuRBO (trust region Bayesian optimization—a technique that intelligently samples promising circuit designs) provides strong initial designs, while multi-task reinforcement learning (a system that learns which designs work best across different operating scenarios) refines them across all variations in voltage, temperature, and manufacturing. Both methods process multiple designs in parallel batches to speed up execution. Additionally, a critic model (a helper that scores designs) prunes away weak candidates, and focused metrics narrow the search to the most promising designs, while simultaneously handling random variations in component behavior.
key_novelty: The innovation is combining Bayesian optimization, multi-task reinforcement learning, and critic-assisted filtering to efficiently design circuits in parallel that stay reliable across all process, voltage, temperature, and manufacturing variations.
contributions: TuRBO-RL framework for PVT-robust analog circuit synthesis
Batch-friendly parallel sampling enabling efficient design space exploration
Critic-assisted pruning and zoom target metrics for sample and time efficiency
Support for simultaneous PVT variation and random mismatch optimization
